newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's Kamchatka hit by sinking of fuel tanker.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Kamchatka hit by sinking of fuel tanker.

text.p: Authorities in Russia's Kamchatka peninsula will introduce partial power cuts to houses and industry from Wednesday after the sinking of a tanker carrying heavy fuel supplies to the far eastern region.
An official with the local administration said by telephone on Monday that power cuts had not yet been introduced, but would be inevitable after Orthodox Christmas on Tuesday.
The next heavy fuel delivery to the peninsula was expected on January 17 or 18, the official said.
More than 400,000 people live in Kamchatka, which is more than 7,000 km (4,375 miles) east of Moscow and nine time zones away.

The 26-year-old tanker Nakhodka, carrying 19,000 tonnes (133,000 barrels) of heavy fuel oil for Kamchatka's power stations, was torn into two and sank last Thursday in the Sea of Japan, spilling some of the fuel.
The spill threatens rich fishing grounds off Japan's main island of Honshu and Japanese maritime authorities made little headway on Monday in their bid to break it up.
